terms.means: The game, and the ball itself. In Melbourne, Adelaide and Perth it means Aussie rules. In Sydney and Brisbane it often means rugby league, so people there say 'the AFL'.
terms.use: You going to the footy on Saturday?

terms.means: To support a team. 'Who do you barrack for?' is the first question anyone asks.
terms.use: I barrack for Geelong, but the rest of my family's Hawthorn.

terms.means: Come on! The classic barracking cry, as in 'Carn the Blues!' or 'Carn, boys!'
terms.use: Carn, boys, one more goal and we're home!

terms.means: What the crowd yells when a player is tackled with the ball. Short for 'holding the ball', which should be a free kick to the tackler.
terms.use: Whole crowd screamed 'Ball!' and the ump just waved play on.

terms.means: The umpires. Footy has umpires, never referees.
terms.use: The umps have had a shocker. Missed three holding-the-balls in one quarter.

terms.means: The MCG, the Melbourne Cricket Ground. Footy's biggest ground and home of the Grand Final.
terms.use: Ninety thousand at the G on a Friday night. Best atmosphere in the country.

terms.means: A spectacular high mark, often taken sitting on someone's shoulders. Also called a hanger.
terms.use: Did you see that screamer in the last quarter? Sat right on his head.

terms.means: Short for a spectacular mark. Same thing as a screamer. Also spelt 'specky'.
terms.use: Took a speccy over three blokes, then missed the set shot.

terms.means: An ugly, wobbly kick that somehow still goes where it's meant to. Said with a laugh when one goes through.
terms.use: Mongrel punt from forty, wobbled the whole way, and it still snuck through.

terms.means: Five or more goals by one player in a game. 'A bag of six' means six.
terms.use: He kicked a bag on Saturday. Five, and two of them from the boundary.

terms.means: A goal, worth six points.
terms.use: Two majors in the first five minutes and the crowd was up and about.

terms.means: One point: the ball goes between a goal post and the shorter behind post, or hits a goal post. A goal is six.
terms.use: Two goals and nine behinds for the half. Can't kick straight to save themselves.

terms.means: A shot that hits the goal post. It only counts as a behind.
terms.use: Hit the post from fifteen metres out. A poster, of all things.

terms.means: A bad mistake: a dropped mark, a kick straight to the other side.
terms.use: Two clangers in a row and the coach had him on the bench.

terms.means: The premiership. Winning the Grand Final is winning the flag.
terms.use: Honestly, I reckon they're good enough to win the flag this year.

terms.means: The Grand Final, usually on the last Saturday in September at the MCG.
terms.use: Who are you tipping for the granny?

terms.means: Finals time. 'Playing in September' means making the finals.
terms.use: None of this matters if we're not there in September.

terms.means: New in 2026: the sides that finish seventh to tenth play off for the last two finals spots, while the top six get a week off.
terms.use: Scraped into the wildcard round on percentage. I'll take it.

terms.means: The league table.
terms.use: Halfway up the ladder and still no idea how good they are.

terms.means: Points scored divided by points conceded, times 100. It splits teams on the same wins, so big wins matter.
terms.use: We need to belt someone to get the percentage up.

terms.means: The Brownlow Medal for the best and fairest player of the season, voted by the umpires. Also called 'Charlie'.
terms.use: He's a big chance in the Brownlow this year if the umps have noticed him.

terms.means: A torpedo punt: a spiralling kick that goes a mile when it comes off.
terms.use: Went for the torp from sixty and it sailed straight through.

terms.means: A kick off the outside of the boot that curls in, used from tight angles near the boundary. Also called a checkside.
terms.use: Banana from right on the boundary line. Unbelievable goal.

terms.means: A quick shot at goal on the run, kicked across the body or over the shoulder.
terms.use: Snapped it over his shoulder from the pocket. Didn't even look.

terms.means: A shot at goal from a mark or free kick, with time to line it up.
terms.use: Missed three set shots from straight in front. Can't have that.

terms.means: A shot at goal taken after the final siren, because the mark or free kick came just before it. In a close game, everything rides on it.
terms.use: After the siren, thirty metres out, and he nailed it. Best thing I've ever seen.

terms.means: A 50-metre penalty: the free kick moves 50 metres closer to goal, often for back-chat or not standing the mark.
terms.use: Gave away a fifty for mouthing off at the ump. Free goal.

terms.means: Picking the winner of every game each round, in an office, family or pub comp. Mostly for bragging rights.
terms.use: I'm dead last in the office tipping. Again.

terms.means: The end of a game that's already decided. Goals then only change the margin.
terms.use: Two junk-time goals made the margin look a lot better than it was.

terms.means: Winning the ball in a tough contest, under real pressure.
terms.use: Great hard-ball get, then a quick handball out of trouble. That's his game.

terms.means: The team things that never make the highlights: spoils, smothers, shepherds.
terms.use: Didn't get much of the ball, but his one-percenters were huge.

terms.means: A casual kick of the footy with mates, in the park or the street. Some grounds let fans on after the game for one.
terms.use: We used to do kick-to-kick in the street till it got too dark to see.

terms.means: Taken off and sat on the bench by the coach, usually straight after a mistake.
terms.use: One more clanger like that and he'll be dragged.

terms.means: Getting hit in the face by the ball.
terms.use: Copped a falcon from his own teammate's handball. Whole crowd winced.

terms.means: Fake one way and go the other, leaving the tackler grabbing at nothing.
terms.use: Sold candy to two of them and kicked the goal. Lovely stuff.

open.m: The safest opener there is. Let them tell you how they feel before you commit to anything.
Open-ended. Works after a win, a loss or a weird one.

open.t: Who do you barrack for, anyway?
open.m: The first question in any footy chat. 'Who do you go for?' works too.

open.t: Get to the footy on the weekend?
open.m: 'The footy' is the game you go to. A good Monday-morning opener at work.

open.t: Only caught the highlights. How'd they go?
open.m: An honest cover if you missed it. 'How'd they go?' gets them telling the whole story.
Footy games often turn late, so there's nearly always a last quarter worth talking about.
The office opener. Everyone's in a comp, and everyone's got a tip they regret.

opinion.t: You've got to win the contested ball. It all starts there.
opinion.m: The all-purpose take. True of almost every game, win or lose.

opinion.t: Too many behinds. Kick straight and it's a different game.
opinion.m: Most teams spray a few shots at goal, so this fits most games.

opinion.t: Too many turnovers coming out of the back half.
opinion.m: Kicking it to the other side near your own goal. Every fan moans about it.

opinion.t: When they bring the pressure, they win. Simple as that.
opinion.m: Tackling and chasing. Hard to argue with.

opinion.t: The forwards need to give the mids something to kick to.
opinion.m: Blames the forward line for not leading into space. Fits a low-scoring game.

opinion.t: Umpiring's been all over the place this year.
opinion.m: A safe complaint any time, about any game.

opinion.t: Nobody remembers the home-and-away. It's what you do in September.
opinion.m: A calm take for a rough patch in the regular rounds.

agree.m: Strong Australian agreement without adding anything you'd have to back up.
Polite agreement. They've made a fair point.
Full agreement. Nod while you say it.
Agreeing with a hint of 'unfortunately'. Good after a loss.
A shrug that fits any strange result or bounce of the ball.
Shared pain. Works after a frustrating game.

dodge.t: I only caught the last quarter. What happened early?
dodge.m: Admit you saw part of it and hand them the floor.
Pushes any prediction off to the finals.

dodge.t: I've stopped tipping them. Every time I do, they lose.
dodge.m: A joking way out of 'will they win next week?'

dodge.t: Haven't looked at the ladder. Too scared.
dodge.m: Gets you out of finals maths.

dodge.t: You'd know better than me. What do you reckon?
dodge.m: Flatter them and bounce the question back.
Fits any team and any prediction, and commits to nothing.

telly.m: When an opposition player gets tackled with the ball. The whole ground yells it.
Come on! Any time your side needs a lift.
When an opponent pushes your player in the back in a marking contest and the ump doesn't pay it.
Any decision that goes the other way.
When your player hasn't seen the tackler coming.
When your side keeps going sideways in defence.
During a set shot at goal, through gritted teeth.

telly.t: Ump, are you watching the same game?
telly.m: When the free kicks start going against you.

exit.t: Anyway, I'll let you go. Catch ya.
Well, there's always next week. See ya.
exit.m: Works after a loss and ends on an upbeat note.

exit.t: I'm grabbing a beer. You right for a drink?
exit.m: 'You right?' means 'do you need anything?' A friendly way out at the pub.

exit.t: Early start tomorrow, so I'm off. Same again next week.
exit.m: Polite exit that promises a rematch.

exit.t: Righto, I'll leave you to it. Go {team}.
exit.m: 'Righto' means 'okay then'. Ends on team loyalty.

exit.t: Long season. We'll see. Take it easy.
exit.m: A noncommittal sign-off that fits any result.

win.open: Good win {when}. Four points in the bank.
win.them: Yeah, wasn't pretty, but they got the job done.
win.back: Won the contested ball and finally hit the scoreboard. That's all you can ask.
win.agree: Spot on. Bank it and move on.
win.exit: Let's see if they can string a few together. Catch ya.

loss.them: Don't. They were off from the first bounce.
loss.back: Got smashed at the stoppages and couldn't hit a target going forward.
loss.agree: Yeah, you can't give {opp} that much of the ball.
loss.exit: That's footy. There's always next week. See ya.

bigWin.them: What a belting. {opp} were cooked by half-time.
bigWin.back: Everyone got on the end of something. And the percentage will thank us come September.
bigWin.agree: Too right. Enjoy it while it lasts.
bigWin.exit: Back to earth next week, probably. Catch ya.

bigLoss.open: So... {score}. You sit through all of that?
bigLoss.them: Turned it off at three-quarter time. Embarrassing.
bigLoss.back: Nobody turned up. And the percentage has copped a hiding, too.
bigLoss.agree: Yeah, fair. The whole side was off.
bigLoss.exit: Best thing is to pretend that never happened. See ya.

narrowWin.open: {score} {when}. Bit close for comfort, wasn't it?
narrowWin.them: Close? I watched the last two minutes through my fingers.
narrowWin.back: Ugly, but four points is four points.
narrowWin.agree: Exactly. You'll take those come September.
narrowWin.exit: My heart can't take many more of those. Catch ya.

narrowLoss.open: Under a goal {when}. That one hurts.
narrowLoss.them: So close. We had our chances, too.
narrowLoss.back: One more kick goes through and it's a different story.
narrowLoss.agree: Yeah, it came down to a couple of moments.
narrowLoss.exit: No point dwelling on it. Next week. See ya.

draw.open: A draw {when}. Not sure how to feel about that.
draw.them: Same. Feels like a win and a loss at the same time.
draw.back: Two points each. Better than nothing, I suppose.
draw.agree: Yeah, I'll take the two points.
draw.exit: Don't see too many of those. Anyway, catch ya.

comeback.open: Behind at three-quarter time and they still got up {when}!
comeback.them: I'd written them off. Didn't think they had it in them.
comeback.back: That last quarter was something else. They just took the game on.
comeback.agree: That's the kind of win that builds belief.
comeback.exit: I'm going to watch that last quarter again. Catch ya.

blewLead.open: How'd we lose that {when}? Three goals up at the last change.
blewLead.them: Classic. Went into their shells and tried to hang on.
blewLead.back: Stopped taking the game on. {opp} kept coming and we just sat back.
blewLead.agree: Exactly. You've got to keep kicking goals.
blewLead.exit: I need a few days to get over that one. See ya.

bagWin.them: Couldn't miss, could he? Every time he went near it, it went through.
bagWin.back: Whenever it went inside fifty, you just knew he'd get on the end of it.
bagWin.agree: Days like that, you just keep kicking it to him.
bagWin.exit: Hope he keeps it going. Catch ya.

finalWin.open: How good was that {when}? Finals footy, mate. Nothing like it.
finalWin.them: I've still got no voice. What a game.
finalWin.back: {player} stood up when it mattered. That's what you need in September.
finalWin.agree: Spot on. Big games, big players.
finalWin.exit: I'm watching the replay again tonight. See ya.

finalLoss.them: Gutted. Couldn't get our hands on the ball.
finalLoss.back: The pressure's another level in September. {opp} handled it better.
finalLoss.agree: Yeah, fair. They were harder at it.
finalLoss.exit: Whatever happens now, it's been a good year. Catch ya.

rivalWin.open: Beat {opp} {when}. Best win of the year.
rivalWin.them: Ha! I've been giving it to a mate who barracks for them all morning.
rivalWin.back: Nothing better. Those games always feel bigger. The crowd's different.
rivalWin.agree: Too right. Bragging rights for months.
rivalWin.exit: I'm off to find someone in the other colours. Catch ya.

rivalLoss.open: Lost to {opp} {when}. Of all the teams.
rivalLoss.them: Don't. I'll never hear the end of it at work.
rivalLoss.back: We'll get 'em next time. I've got it circled already.
rivalLoss.agree: They'd better be ready, that's all I'll say.
rivalLoss.exit: Keeping my head down for a few days. See ya.

pub.say: BALL! How's that not holding the ball?
o: He had all day to get rid of it. Ump's having a shocker.
Backs the crowd and blames the umpire. Exactly what everyone around you is doing.
Maybe he didn't have prior opportunity?
You might even be right, but defending the umpire at the footy is a lonely place.
Which ball? Isn't there only one?
'Ball!' is the crowd's shout for holding the ball. Everyone knows it.

pub.say: Did you see that screamer in the second quarter?
o: Sat right on his shoulders. Mark of the year, that.
A screamer is a huge high mark. Praise it like you saw it live.
Yeah, great catch.
Close, but in footy it's a mark, not a catch.
Who was screaming? The crowd?
A screamer is a spectacular mark, not a noise.

pub.say: He kicked a bag on the weekend.
o: His conversion rate was well above his season average.
Maybe, but nobody talks like a stats sheet at the pub.
A bag of what?
A bag is five or more goals. Asking gives you away.
Five, wasn't it? Couldn't miss.
Knows what a bag is and sounds like you saw it.

pub.say: Mongrel punt, but they all count.
o: Ugliest goal of the year. Still six points.
Laugh along. A goal's a goal, however it gets there.
His kicking technique needs a bit of work.
Fair enough, but flat. The fun is that it went through anyway.
Why'd he punt it? Was it fourth down?
That's American football. In footy a punt is just a kind of kick.

pub.say: Who do you reckon wins the flag next year?
o: Whoever finishes top of the ladder.
Not how it works. The flag goes to whoever wins the Grand Final.
Ask me in September. Depends who's fit.
Sounds seasoned and commits to nothing.
What flag? Like a national flag?
The flag is the premiership. Every fan knows it.

pub.say: You in the tipping comp this year?
o: Course. Second-last, but I'm due.
Being hopeless at tipping is a proud tradition.
I don't really gamble.
Fair enough, but tipping is just picking winners for bragging rights.
Tipping? Like at a restaurant?
Footy tipping means picking the winners each round.
Barrack? Like an army barracks?
To barrack is to support a team. It's the most basic footy question there is.
{team}. For my sins.
Name your team with a sigh. Very Australian.
Bit of everyone, really.
Nobody barracks for everyone. Pick a side.

pub.say: Four goals down at three-quarter time and we still got up!
o: Unreal last quarter. I'd given up on them.
'Got up' means won. Share the relief.
Twenty-four points isn't that much in footy.
True, a four-goal lead can go fast. But it kills the moment.
Wait, they stop after three quarters?
Three-quarter time is just the last break. There are four quarters.

avoid.why: Footy has umpires, never referees. 'Ref' marks you as a rugby or soccer person.
'Root' is rude slang in Australia. You barrack for, or go for, a team.
Footy has finals, played in September. 'Playoffs' sounds American.

avoid.instead: they won the flag (or the premiership)
avoid.why: The winners are the premiers, and fans talk about winning the flag.
The league table is the ladder.
A score like 14.12 (96) means 14 goals and 12 behinds, 96 points. The dot isn't read as 'point'.
Catching a kick is taking a mark. 'Catch' sounds like cricket.
Fans say the last quarter. The breaks are quarter-time, half-time and three-quarter time.
Footy players wear jumpers. Commentators call them guernseys.
Tries are rugby. In footy you kick goals, worth six, and behinds, worth one.

nerd: If you look at the numbers, we were plus-fifteen in contested possessions and won the clearances, but we only scored from about one in three inside-fifties, so honestly the margin flatters them.
offq: Do you reckon they'll play two rucks next year, or keep the backup in the twos?

builtin.label: AFL (Aussie rules)
betting: Several bets rolled into one. Every leg has to come in, and it's always the last one that busts.
A multi inside one game: the winner, the margin, a player to kick a goal.
A straight bet on who wins.
A points start for the underdog, so both sides pay about the same.
Pick the winner, and whether they win by 1 to 39 points or by 40 or more.
Have a bet. Careful: in footy a punt is also a kick.

unsure: 2026 Grand Final checked: Brisbane Lions 14.12 (96) beat Fremantle 12.17 (89) at the MCG on 26 September 2026 (AFL.com.au, Reuters via The Star, FootyInfo), Brisbane's third flag in a row. Nothing in the pack depends on it.

'the eight' (the top eight): left out. Since the 2026 wildcard round (top ten play finals, top six get a week off), media talk is of the top six and the wildcard spots, and it isn't clear 'make the eight' has survived.
carn: Wiktionary (with a Herald Sun headline as a citation) is the only written source found, though it's familiar from club banners and crowds.
avoid 'the fourth quarter': based on usage (AFL.com.au and ABC say 'last quarter', 'final term' and 'the last change'); no source calls 'fourth quarter' wrong, and some people do say it.
avoid 'root for': from general Australian English, not a footy source.
'footy' meaning rugby league in Sydney and Brisbane is from Wiktionary; how far AFL fans there say 'footy' for AFL among themselves varies.
betting: 'same-game multi' and 'big win, little win' come from bookmaker and betting-guide pages, not independent journalism. 'The line' wording is general, not a quoted definition.
terms left out: 'sausage roll' and 'snag' (rhyming slang for a goal) may be dated; 'maggot' for umpires is too insulting; 'leather poisoning' had only one source.
ipa for 'the Brownlow' was written from the standard pronunciation (no dictionary entry). 'Brownlow night' timing wasn't confirmed for 2026, so the term doesn't give a date.
sources: The Age, the Herald Sun, Fox Footy, news.com.au and the SMH refuse this research tool, so none were read directly. ABC pages were read with curl.
